title: A map from a compact object into a nicely filtered dg module factors through a finitely filtered submodule
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file dga.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-factor-through-nicer at source lines 6433-6451: for a differential graded algebra A, a compact object E of D(A,d), a dg A-module P with a finite filtration whose successive quotients are direct sums of shifted copies of A, and a morphism E -> P in the derived category, there is a dg submodule P' of P whose successive quotients are finite direct sums of the same shifts and through which E -> P factors. The proof at source lines 6453-6495 is an induction that has to carry three properties simultaneously and is not a routine application of compactness. It strengthens the statement to an induction on the level m of the filtration with the hypotheses that F_m P is contained in P', that all higher quotients are finite direct sums of the prescribed shifts, and that the given map factors through P'. The induction step chooses homogeneous generators of the graded pieces, writes the differential of each generator as a sum of other generators plus a term pushed down to the previous level, uses the finiteness of the image of that pushed-down term to bound the required summands at level m-1, forms the inverse image of that finite sum as the new P'', and then has to invoke compactness of E to enlarge the finite index set until the map factors through the enlarged module, all while preserving the quotient description. The three properties interact at every step and the statement mentions none of the bookkeeping.
